content.value_statement: Vue projects become difficult when reactivity, component boundaries, and data flow are inconsistent. This skill applies structured Vue 3 guidance throughout implementation and review.
actual_capabilities: Guides Vue 3 Composition API and TypeScript component structure.
Plans focused component boundaries before non-trivial implementation.
Reviews refs, reactive state, computed values, and watchers.
Defines typed props, emits, models, and provide-inject contracts.
Selects suitable composables, built-in components, directives, and plugins.
Recommends list, memoization, animation, and update performance practices.
limitations: Assumes Vue 3 and prefers Composition API unless the project explicitly requires another style.
Provides reference guidance and does not install dependencies or execute application code.
Does not replace project tests, accessibility review, or browser verification.
Performance recommendations still require measurements against the actual application.

use_cases.title: Modernize Vue Components
use_cases.description: Refactor existing components into typed Composition API structures with clearer state and responsibilities.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Architecture
use_cases.description: Establish consistent component boundaries, data flow, composables, and file organization across a Vue codebase.

use_cases.title: Improve Rendering Performance
use_cases.description: Review large lists, update hooks, memoization, and animation choices after application behavior is correct.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Vue component for Composition API structure, reactivity, template safety, and clear props and emits. Explain the most important changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of an existing single-file component

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this Vue feature into focused components and composables. Preserve behavior, define typed contracts, and explain each responsibility boundary.

prompt_templates.title: Design Component Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a component map for this Vue requirement. Define responsibilities, state ownership, props, emits, composables, and optional framework features.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Vue workflow for rendering costs. Prioritize measured bottlenecks involving lists, updates, memoization, async components, and state-driven animations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced performance review after functionality is verified

output_examples.input: Review a large product page component that handles filters, fetching, results, and status controls.
output: A component map separates orchestration, filters, results, and status controls.
A composable owns fetching, state, cancellation, and derived values.
Typed props and emits define each child component contract.

output_examples.input: Improve a slow Vue list containing thousands of interactive rows.
output: Profile rendering before changing the component structure.
Virtualize visible rows and retain stable item keys.
Use memoization only for subtrees with stable, measurable dependencies.

output_examples.input: Review state shared between components in an SSR application.
output_examples.output: The review identifies unsafe module state, recommends request-scoped stores, and documents typed injection boundaries.

best_practices: Confirm the existing Vue architecture and project conventions before changing code.
Keep source state minimal and derive values with pure computed properties.
Measure behavior and performance before applying optional optimizations.
anti_patterns: Do not place orchestration, state, and several independent interfaces in one large component.
Do not use watchers to maintain values that computed properties can derive.
Do not add advanced Vue features without a clear product or technical requirement.

faq.question: Does this skill support Vue 2?
faq.answer: It targets Vue 3. Vue 2 projects need framework-specific guidance and compatibility review.

faq.question: Can it work with the Options API?
faq.answer: It prefers Composition API. It defers to explicit project requirements and recommends separate Options API guidance.

faq.question: Does it generate complete Vue features?
faq.answer: It can guide implementation and review, but requirements, project context, tests, and verification remain necessary.

faq.question: Does it cover state management?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares local composables, Pinia, and small global state patterns while warning about SSR singleton state.

faq.question: Does it cover Vue performance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers virtualization, memoization, component overhead, update hooks, and animation choices after behavior is correct.

faq.question: Will it install Vue packages?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples but does not install dependencies or execute project commands.
